whatThePageStates: The page carries two Region-availability matrices. The first (introduced by "which Region-specific endpoints are supported by directory type") has 38 Region rows and four directory-type columns: AWS Managed Microsoft AD (Standard and Enterprise Editions), AWS Managed Microsoft AD (Hybrid Edition), AD Connector, and Simple AD. Every cell is an explicit Yes or No icon plus word, so non-support is stated, not merely absent. The second table, under the heading "Supported AWS Regions for Directory Service Data", has 18 Region rows and three directory-type columns for the separate ds-data endpoint: AWS Managed Microsoft AD, AD Connector, Simple AD. The remaining prose is three cross-references (GovCloud endpoints, China endpoints, FIPS endpoints) and the boilerplate "See also" note about AI coding assistant skills; neither table states anything about resource types or about other AWS services.

shouldNotExtract: The Region name, Region, Endpoint and Protocol columns are keys and metadata, not coverage: 'ds.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com' and 'HTTPS' are never Yes/No values, and Protocol is the literal string HTTPS in all 56 rows. The icon-yes and icon-no PNG image links are rendering artefacts of the Yes/No words, not separate values. The three trailing cross-reference paragraphs (GovCloud (US) service endpoints, Endpoints and ARNs for Amazon Web Services in China, and twice the Directory Service Data endpoints and quotas FIPS pointer) are pointers to other pages and state no availability here; in particular the FIPS sentences must not be turned into a FIPS-endpoint coverage claim, because this page lists no FIPS endpoints. The '## See also' bullet about AI coding assistant skills and the 'aws agent-toolkit search-skills' command is boilerplate. The <a name=...> anchors and the two section headings are structure, not data.
coverageDimensions: REGION: fully supplied. 38 named Region codes for the Directory Service control plane and 18 named Region codes for Directory Service Data, each with a stated Yes or No per directory type; the union of both tables is 38 distinct Regions, and the 18 Directory Service Data Regions are a subset of the 38. Partitions are mixed into the same list (2 China Regions and 2 GovCloud Regions among the 38), so a partition figure can be derived only by reading Region codes, and the page never uses the word partition. SERVICE: none. The page is about a single service, AWS Directory Service, plus its Directory Service Data API; it does not enumerate AWS services and supports no 'N services covered' figure. RESOURCE TYPE: none. The columns are directory types (product editions and offerings such as Simple AD and AD Connector), not resource types, and no ARN type, CloudFormation type or API resource is named anywhere on the page. Any resourceType number attributed to this page would be fabricated.
trap: The single most likely misparse is collapsing the page to one number: reporting 'AWS Directory Service is available in 38 Regions' (or in 56, by adding the two tables) and discarding the per-directory-type split. That loses 11 stated Hybrid Edition exclusions, 32 stated Simple AD exclusions, and 36 stated Directory Service Data exclusions. Runners-up: (a) double counting the 18 Directory Service Data Regions as new Regions when all 18 are already in the first table; (b) treating the second table's 'AWS Managed Microsoft AD' column as the same capability as the first table's 'AWS Managed Microsoft AD (Standard and Enterprise Editions)' column and merging 18 rows into 38; (c) dropping the two all-No Directory Service Data columns as empty, which converts 36 explicit No values into silence; (d) harvesting the Endpoint or Protocol column as a coverage value, which yields 38 or 56 phantom 'HTTPS' hits; (e) reading the icon image alt-less tags as blank cells and inferring Partial where the page only ever states Yes or No - there is no tri-state anywhere on this page; (f) turning the FIPS or GovCloud cross-reference sentences into availability claims.
